co_boulder_slips.blurb: A small roadside crag high in Boulder Canyon, just beyond the Boulder Falls trail. Roughly two dozen single-pitch lines run from about 40 to 125 feet on granite, with trad leading the way and a handful of bolted sport lines and one top-rope option. Grades start near 5.6 and top out in the low 5.14s, but most of the climbing sits between 5.9 and 5.11. Expect slabs, corners, aretes, cracks and a steep thin-crack wall. Protection on some of the older trad lines is sparse, so it suits climbers comfortable placing small gear. The crag is quiet, with very little walking required.
co_boulder_slips.parking_note: Leave the car at the gravel pullout on the canyon road just past the Boulder Falls trail turnoff.
co_boulder_slips.approach: From the roadside pullout, right-hand routes are about a minute up to a wooded shoulder; the left side takes roughly five minutes on a steep, loose dirt path.

co_anarchy_wall_2.blurb: A steep, bolted wall on the south side of the highway in Clear Creek Canyon near Golden, built for strong sport climbers. Most of the lines are single-pitch sport routes graded 5.12 and 5.13, with a couple of easier pitches in the 5.7 to 5.8 range and a few boulder problems. The rock is clean but holds tend to be slopey, which gets worse when it is hot, so cooler or shaded hours work better. Some routes have awkward clips. Top-roping is a poor fit, and the approach is quick.
co_anarchy_wall_2.parking_note: Use the pullout on the south side of the highway right after the third tunnel.
co_anarchy_wall_2.approach: A short walk east and slightly uphill from the pullout leads to the overhanging wall.

co_east_ironing_board.blurb: A four-humped fin of rock in the Flatirons, the first big formation west of the Third Flatiron above Boulder. About twenty single-pitch lines, split between trad and bolted sport, climb its east and west faces, from easy low-angle terrain through moderate 5.7 cracks and slabs up to hard 5.13 sport. The west face carries the bolts, while the upper end has crack climbing and wants a full rack. It is described as peaceful and rarely crowded, with long views of the Flatirons skyline. The walk in involves a short third-class scramble and some loose rock near the base.
co_east_ironing_board.approach: Hike the Royal Arch Trail from Chautauqua, then leave it at a painted boulder and drop into Bluebell Canyon. A short third-class scramble leads to the base; the west face is reached by switchbacks.

co_atomic_energy_crag.blurb: A remote sandstone cliff in the Naturita and Paradox Valley region of western Colorado, with a mix of trad and bolted sport lines of roughly 50 to 70 feet. Grades run from the 5.7 range to 5.12, with the bulk of the climbing at 5.10 and 5.11, plus a single hard boulder problem on the blocks at the base. The stone is good-quality Dakota sandstone and the wall catches plenty of sun, making fall, winter and spring the comfortable seasons. There are enough lines for a few days, and camping is possible beneath the cliff.

co_sunshine_wall_2.blurb: A bouldering wall on the south side of Turtle Rock, near Buena Vista at roughly 8,250 feet. Twenty-two problems line a slightly overhung corridor just a few steps from the parking area, mostly in the V2 to V6 range with an easy start and one or two harder lines. The corridor is usually in the sun, which feels good in cold months but can be too hot in summer, and wind either gets blocked or funnels through. It makes a sociable spot with room to hang out. One problem on the far west end has a tall, scary top-out.
co_sunshine_wall_2.parking_note: From Buena Vista, head east on Main Street, turn left on North Colorado Avenue and follow the county roads past the tunnels to Turtle Rock; park on the east side of the rock.
co_sunshine_wall_2.approach: A very short walk southwest from the parking area, then west into the corridor.

co_punchbowl_the.blurb: A limestone sport crag on the east side of Lime Creek canyon, in the high country above Eagle at over 9,000 feet. The area is named for a cave whose bowl sometimes fills with runoff. Every route is bolted, and about two dozen lines mostly sit in the 5.11 and 5.12 range, with a couple of 5.13s and a few easier warm-ups in the 5.7 to 5.10 range. Some lines are in the cave and others in the trees to its left. Good protection and a quick walk in make it a practical day for harder sport climbers.
co_punchbowl_the.approach: Where the east access road ends, a brief path heads straight to the crag.
